title: Software Engineer
summary: Designs, builds, tests, and improves software for web, mobile, and devices.
description: Software engineers solve real-world problems by writing and maintaining code. They collaborate with designers and product teams, build features, fix bugs, and ensure performance and security. Roles range from front-end to back-end to full-stack, across many industries.

high_school: Take math through Calculus if possible; complete AP CS A or equivalent.
Participate in coding competitions or robotics; publish projects on GitHub.
Pursue a summer coding camp or online course to deepen skills.
post_secondary: Major in CS/Software Engineering or related; complete internships.
Master data structures, algorithms, web dev, databases, cloud fundamentals.
early_career: Target junior SWE roles; continue learning frameworks and writing tests.

title: Data Scientist
summary: Extracts insights from data using statistics, programming, and machine learning.
description: Data scientists clean, analyze, and model data to answer questions and guide decisions. They work across domains—from sports to healthcare—using tools like Python, SQL, and visualization libraries. Communication is key to explain findings to non-technical audiences.

high_school: Take math through Calculus and Statistics; learn basic Python.
Join data or math clubs; explore mini-projects (e.g., sports stats).
post_secondary: Pursue Data Science/Statistics/CS; complete internships involving data.
Learn ML fundamentals, practical SQL, dashboards, and experiment design.
early_career: Start as Data Analyst/Junior DS; build a portfolio of end-to-end projects.

title: Cybersecurity Analyst
summary: Protects systems and data by detecting, preventing, and responding to threats.
description: Cybersecurity analysts monitor networks, investigate alerts, and harden defenses to keep organizations safe. They develop playbooks, conduct risk assessments, and help users follow secure practices. Certifications and labs are common on-ramps to the field.

high_school: Build fundamentals: OS, networking, basic scripting.
Join a CTF team; practice safe labs and virtual machines.
post_secondary: Study Cybersecurity/IT/CS; pursue labs/internships.
Learn threat detection, incident response, and secure configuration.
early_career: Target SOC analyst/help desk → analyst; continue cert progression.

title: Biomedical Engineer
summary: Applies engineering to healthcare—devices, imaging, and biomaterials.
description: Biomedical engineers bridge engineering and medicine to design devices like prosthetics, improve imaging systems like MRI and CT, and develop biomaterials. They collaborate with clinicians and researchers to improve patient outcomes and safety.

high_school: Complete strong science/math sequence; join engineering/science clubs.
Shadow non-clinical biomedical departments if possible.
post_secondary: Major in Biomedical Engineering (ABET-accredited if possible).
Pursue labs/internships with device companies or research groups.
early_career: Target roles in device testing, quality, or junior R&D assistance.

title: Robotics Engineer
summary: Designs and builds robotic systems integrating mechanics, electronics, and software.
description: Robotics engineers blend mechanical design, electronics, and programming to create automated systems. Work includes CAD, prototyping, sensors, and control systems—spanning manufacturing, healthcare, and exploration.

high_school: Build simple robots; learn CAD and basic electronics.
Compete in robotics; document projects in a portfolio.
post_secondary: Major in Mechanical/Mechatronics/Robotics Engineering.
Intern with automation/manufacturing labs; learn control theory.
early_career: Start in test/assembly/automation tech roles; grow into design engineering.

title: Environmental Scientist
summary: Studies the natural world to protect ecosystems, air, water, and soil quality.
description: Environmental scientists collect and analyze data about the environment to identify hazards, monitor ecosystems, and develop solutions. They work in the field and in labs for government agencies, nonprofits, and consulting firms.

high_school: Take Biology, Chemistry, and Environmental Science.
Participate in citizen science or environmental volunteer projects.
post_secondary: Major in Environmental Science, Biology, or Earth Science.
Pursue field internships with agencies or nonprofits.
early_career: Enter as environmental technician or field researcher.

title: UX/UI Designer
summary: Designs digital experiences that are useful, accessible, and delightful to use.
description: UX/UI designers research user needs, prototype interfaces, and iterate based on testing and feedback. They work across apps, websites, and devices, bridging visual design with the technical world. Empathy and curiosity are as important as visual skills.

high_school: Develop visual design and web skills; build a personal portfolio.
Redesign an existing app for fun—document your process.
post_secondary: Study HCI, Interaction Design, or Graphic Design with digital focus.
Intern at product companies; build real case studies.
early_career: Start as junior UX researcher or product designer; grow into senior roles.

title: AI / Machine Learning Engineer
summary: Builds intelligent systems that learn from data to make predictions and decisions.
description: AI and ML engineers design, train, and deploy models that power everything from recommendation systems to medical diagnostics. They combine software engineering with statistical modeling, working closely with data scientists and product teams.

high_school: Excel in Calculus and Statistics; learn Python fundamentals.
Explore ML through online courses (e.g., fast.ai, Kaggle Learn).
post_secondary: Major in CS, Math, or Data Science with AI/ML electives.
Complete research internships; build projects on public datasets.
early_career: Enter as ML engineer or AI researcher; specialize in a domain.

title: Network Engineer
summary: Designs and manages the infrastructure that connects computers and the internet.
description: Network engineers build and maintain the systems that keep data flowing—routers, switches, firewalls, and cloud networks. They troubleshoot outages, optimize performance, and plan for growth. It's a field where deep technical skill meets critical thinking.

high_school: Learn OS fundamentals and basic networking; set up a home lab.
Volunteer for IT support; pursue free Cisco NetAcad courses.
post_secondary: Study Computer Networking or IT; earn foundational certifications.
Intern with IT departments or MSPs.
early_career: Start as network technician or IT support; progress to administration.

title: Bioinformatics Scientist
summary: Uses computing to analyze biological data—genomes, proteins, and beyond.
description: Bioinformatics scientists sit at the intersection of biology, computer science, and statistics. They develop pipelines to process genomic data, identify disease markers, and accelerate drug discovery. This fast-growing field blends lab science with serious coding skills.

high_school: Strengthen biology and CS fundamentals simultaneously.
Explore genomics databases (e.g., NCBI) for self-directed projects.
post_secondary: Major in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, or CS+Biology.
Work in a research lab; learn pipeline tools and cloud computing.
early_career: Enter as bioinformatics analyst or research computing assistant.

title: Civil Engineer
summary: Designs infrastructure that supports communities—roads, bridges, water, and buildings.
description: Civil engineers plan and oversee construction of public and private infrastructure, ensuring safety, sustainability, and compliance. They collaborate with surveyors, architects, and contractors and often specialize in structural, environmental, transportation, or geotechnical fields.

high_school: Build strong math and science fundamentals; practice problem-solving and project sketches.
Join clubs that involve design, construction, or community service projects.
post_secondary: Pursue an ABET-accredited Civil Engineering degree and complete internships.
Gain experience with CAD, site design, construction materials, and codes.
early_career: Start as EIT/engineering intern; obtain Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) license.
Work on supervised design and field inspection to earn Professional Engineer (PE) eligibility.

title: Chemical Engineer
summary: Transforms raw materials into products through chemistry, processes, and equipment.
description: Chemical engineers design processes for producing chemicals, pharmaceuticals, fuels, and materials while ensuring safety and efficiency. They apply principles of chemistry, thermodynamics, and transport phenomena in lab and plant settings.

high_school: Develop strong chemistry and math foundation; take advanced science electives.
Complete lab research or internships in manufacturing labs.
post_secondary: Major in Chemical Engineering and engage in co-op programs.
Learn process design tools, catalysis, and quality control.
Pursue internships with chemical manufacturers or biotech companies.
early_career: Enter as process engineer intern or junior process engineer.
Work in process optimization, scale-up, and plant troubleshooting.

title: Aerospace Engineer
summary: Designs aircraft, spacecraft, satellites, and missiles through advanced engineering.
description: Aerospace engineers develop flight systems, propulsion, and structural components for aviation and space exploration. They run simulations, test prototypes, and collaborate with cross-discipline teams to meet stringent safety and performance requirements.

high_school: Master Physics and Calculus; design model rockets or drones.
Attend aerospace camps and read about flight mechanics.
post_secondary: Major in Aerospace Engineering or Mechanical Engineering with aerospace electives.
Intern with aerospace manufacturers, defense labs, or research groups.
early_career: Start as junior aerospace engineer or test engineer.
Gain experience in CAD, CFD, and certification processes.
